svg.text: Write Confirmation Gate
Two independent locks, and a human between them — the same shape in every plane
Lock 1 — Write opt-in
ENABLE_WRITES / enableWrites
off by default, everywhere
No flag → the tool is not registered at all.
Risk classification
read_public → read_sensitive
→ write_standard → destructive → critical
Unclassified → refuse to start. Fail closed.
Lock 2 — confirm: true at call time
Enforced centrally in withGuardrail(), not by each handler remembering to.
destructive and critical always require it.
Call without confirm
→ returns a PREVIEW
no Graph call is made
logged as confirmation_required
A stopped-at-the-gate write is still an audit event.
Show the preview to a human
"Isolate WIN-ABC123 — device is unmanaged, last seen 9 days."
They see exactly what will change, before anything changes.
Never infer approval from "investigate this" or "make a plan".
An approval is a person clicking yes. Not an inference.
Call again with confirm: true — only after explicit approval
Executes, redacts the response, and writes the audit row with risk level, tool, and outcome.
Tenant allowlist, rate limits, and session expiry still apply on the way through.
The agent can read your directory. It cannot change it without the opt-in AND the click. Under the gateway, a backend
never inherits a write flag from the gateway environment — settings.yaml is the only place it can be turned on.
